fix.shows: PTI sets out the rolls of the five states due to vote early next year, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur and Goa, before the revision, at the draft and at the final roll, from figures the Election Commission and the Chief Electoral Officers published. By its count the five rolls fell from about 18.71 crore to 16.43 crore, a fall of about 2.29 crore or 12.2 per cent, and Uttar Pradesh accounts for nearly 90 per cent of it. It gives the fall in the roll as 13.24 per cent in Uttar Pradesh, 10.76 per cent in Goa, 10.07 per cent in Uttarakhand, 6.34 per cent in Punjab and 6.33 per cent in Manipur. For Uttar Pradesh it gives 15.44 crore electors before the revision, 12.56 crore on the draft and 13.40 crore on the final roll, with about 2.89 crore names left off the draft. PTI says about 0.84 crore of those, roughly 29 per cent, were restored, and it describes about 34 per cent in Punjab, about 17 per cent in Manipur and about 3 per cent in Uttarakhand as names that came back. Each of those figures measures the rise from the draft to the final roll, which is the names added after the draft, new voters among them, less the names deleted after it. The report does not say how many of the names added had been left off the draft. Goa's final roll is smaller than its draft.
